items.title: Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1959-01-02
items.q: many jobs I played in the Papa Salastain Band in my brother John's place.

ctx.x: and I'll just go by that way. I just wonder if it's from the family way back in the colonial times probably. To get on with your musical education, we'll say, when you started on banjo, your brother used to help you. Oh yes. Did you play in a band pretty quick then?

Yeah, yes indeed. I played a band pretty quick. I remember my brother John sent me in his place. He was with Sam Morgan one time ago, he sent me with Sam Morgan and Kid Ora was on trombone. We was advertised in the street then, in trucks. I remember that this guy played in his place and many jobs I played in the Papa Salastain Band in my brother John's place.
Do you remember your very first job? Was that the one you substituted in Morgan's band?

items.title: Alcide "Slow Drag" Pavageau and Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1957-09-01
items.q: Played with Solishtan a long time. John Marrera.

ctx.x: My brother. Which one? John Marrera. You heard talk about John Marrera. He was a leading band you played.
Played with Solishtan a long time. John Marrera. With P. Ron too, didn't he? Yeah. He played with King Joe Oliver. You remember Joe Oliver? Yeah we had the records.

Yeah. And he played with Kid Rene and Buddy Pitty. And he started you on banjo. He started me on banjo. How I started banjo I picked it up to see my mother, she played guitar. My father was a bass player, which you heard about your knowledge. My brother was a bass player and my brother John was a guitar and a banjo player. But they all really was good and I used to listen to them all the time. And my first instrument was a guitar. My first number was Under the Double Eagle. I remember that and I can't play it…
